_comment: Drives `vexpo asc accessibility lint` and `vexpo asc accessibility push`. This is the versioned source for the Accessibility Nutrition Label; push sends it to App Store Connect, and `--publish` moves the draft onto the App Store page. The shape matches Apple's AccessibilityDeclaration: one entry per device family, nine booleans, anything omitted defaults to false. `notes` is ours, not Apple's. Apple's bar is task-based: every common task, which means first launch, sign in, purchase, settings and the app's primary job, has to be completable with the feature turned on. Re-check that against your own screens before you push: your app is not this app.

entries.notes: IPHONE only, because app.config.ts sets supportsTablet: false. Captions and audio descriptions are false because nothing here plays media. What the rest rest on, in the template's own code. supportsVoiceover: every control carries a label, hints on the ones whose label doesn't say what happens, isHeader on screen titles, decorative symbols hidden with accessibilityHidden(true), and errors and successes announced from fail() and succeed() so a repeat is heard as a repeat. supportsVoiceControl: accessibilityInputLabels on the buttons whose visible name is awkward to say. supportsLargerText: useDynamicFont resolves every size to a SwiftUI text style, so text scales through Font.custom(relativeTo:) to 200% and beyond, and icons that would break the layout are capped with dynamicTypeSize rather than pinned. Tab bars and inline nav titles stay fixed, which Apple's own criteria exempt. supportsSufficientContrast: __tests__/lib/contrast.test.ts measures the text pairings at 4.5:1 and the control and border pairings at 3:1, across all four appearances. supportsDifferentiateWithoutColorAlone: status rows pair the colour with a symbol and a word, and no control uses colour as its only state. supportsReducedMotion: a three-way preference over the system setting, read by the screen transitions, the banners, the onboarding bar and the sessions list. Everything above is verified statically: none of it has been heard on a device, and nobody has run Apple's common-task walk with the feature on.
